one_sentence_story: Simultaneous human EEG-fMRI and glymphatic imaging prove that natural slow-wave sleep opens microscopic fluid channels by 60 percent and drives 20-to-50-second blood-vessel waves to wash metabolic waste from your cortex — a pump muted both by conditioned bedroom hyperarousal and by sedative sleeping pills.
so_what_for_you: Trying to force sleep by lying tense in bed wires your mattress into an alarm cue, while knocking yourself out with a sedative sleeping pill flattens the slow vascular pump that actually rinses your brain clean.
